FR-001.title: The evaluation MUST offer an isolated, optional prototype for comparing VibeVoice speech with the existing macOS speech method.

FR-002.title: The prototype MUST be removable or disableable without changing the existing method's behavior or contract.

FR-003.title: The evaluation MUST use the same five permitted texts per language for each feasible configuration and the baseline.

FR-004.title: The evaluation MUST support private listening and individual 1–10 product-owner ratings for English and German samples where feasible.

FR-005.title: The report MUST show individual ratings, averages by language and configuration, and qualitative observations.

FR-006.title: The evaluation MUST identify the exact model variant, voice, language, machine, and configuration for every result.

FR-007.title: The evaluation MUST investigate both identified VibeVoice TTS variants and report any unavailable or unauthorized implementation without claiming a comparison was performed.

FR-008.title: The evaluation MUST report storage, memory, platform details, and applicable requirements for each candidate machine, including the inspection time and the intended storage volume when known.

FR-009.title: The evaluation MUST record installed footprint, peak memory where measurable, and generation time for each evaluated configuration, identifying unavailable measurements and their reasons.

FR-010.title: Before a target-machine download, installation, or service change, the operator MUST obtain explicit approval for that action and destination.

FR-011.title: Before using a model, dependency, voice, or sample text, the evaluation MUST document the applicable terms and determine whether the intended private research use is permitted; unresolved permission MUST block the affected use.

FR-012.title: The evaluation MUST record missing, failed, unsafe, or unavailable comparisons and the reason for each.

FR-013.title: The evaluation MUST keep sample texts, generated audio, and results private unless a separate publication decision authorizes disclosure.

FR-014.title: The evaluation MUST provide the product owner with a recordable decision to retain, partially retain, remove, or seek an alternative.

FR-015.title: The evaluation MUST stop an affected run on failure, cancellation, or an agreed resource limit and report the incomplete result.

decisions.decision: Treat VibeVoice-TTS-1.5B and VibeVoice-Realtime-0.5B as the two candidates, but make no claim that either language or implementation is usable without verification.
decisions.why: Official sources report the 1.5B code removed and German support unqualified; Realtime German is experimental.
decisions.rejected: Assume both candidates can be run for both English and German.

decisions.decision: Keep model execution behind approved local adapters and out of the production backend environment; do not download or install automatically.
decisions.why: Exact implementation, dependency, model, voice, terms, and target capacity require review and approval first.
decisions.rejected: Add model runtimes to the backend lockfile or let the evaluator fetch assets.

decisions.decision: Use the existing authenticated local speech endpoint as the baseline.
decisions.why: It preserves the existing speech contract and avoids duplicating its macOS voice and audio behavior.
decisions.rejected: Call macOS say directly or add a production VibeVoice route.

decisions.decision: Use a loopback-only rating UI and local JSON report with operator-supplied sample texts and output path.
decisions.why: It supports private listening and durable evidence without a hosted service or checked-in private artifacts.
decisions.rejected: Upload results or commit a sample corpus.

decisions.decision: Measure each candidate machine rather than infer suitability from model size or upstream examples.
decisions.why: Upstream reports are not qualification of the actual machines, especially for platform/runtime requirements.
decisions.rejected: Treat upstream benchmarks or parameter count as proof of feasibility.

decisions.decision: Require exact language-tag matches and a baseline on the same machine for every candidate configuration.
decisions.why: This prevents pairing samples or machines that do not provide a valid comparison.
decisions.rejected: Accept language-group-only matches or a baseline from another machine.

decisions.decision: Select VibeVoice Realtime 0.5B for backend integration with `say` as its resource-pressure fallback; use Carter for English and Spk1 for German by default, with Spk0 as an optional German preset.
decisions.why: The VibeVoice voice averages were higher in all three reviewed comparisons, and the same model weights serve both languages.
decisions.rejected: Keep the evaluator as the only VibeVoice use or load separate English and German model instances.

decisions.decision: Exclude unused acoustic-tokenizer encoder components from the serving footprint and yield VibeVoice memory to higher-priority inference workloads.
decisions.why: The inference path uses the tokenizer decoder, and the warm benchmark measured about 7.28 GiB peak process RSS for one full model process.
decisions.rejected: Keep the full model resident regardless of other machine workloads.

plan.summary: Planned a standalone, private VibeVoice comparison harness with explicit permission gates and local reporting.
plan.key_finding: The official 1.5B implementation is disabled and German support is not qualified for either candidate, so unavailable comparisons must remain explicit rather than be substituted.

specify.summary: Completed the private evaluation. Review ratings selected VibeVoice Realtime 0.5B for a lower-priority backend integration with memory yielding and `say` fallback.

approach: Implement an optional standalone evaluator under backend/evaluation/vibevoice. Validate private inputs and terms, inspect the target, run only approved local adapters against the existing local speech API, and preserve paired audio and results in an owner-only local report. Review the report through a loopback-only UI; leave production service behavior and dependencies unchanged, and record unavailable or unsupported comparisons explicitly.
